question: Can exact field gradients reach a fixed, independently validated motor torque-ripple target substantially faster than inexpensive physical models and competitive derivative-free optimization?
decision: Pursue a nonlinear slotted 2D motor pilot. Keep the existing linear slotless motor as a negative control. Do not start a large optimization campaign before forward-model and design-space gates pass.
completed_this_pass: Read existing GEODE magnetostatic, magnetization, torque and motor benchmark source.
Reanalysed committed torque samples with an even-angle training / odd-angle holdout split; see slotless_screen.json.
Inspected two primary motor-adjoint papers and the public ICEM code snapshot prerequisites, optimization setup and available artifacts.
Recorded this question and evidence in the geode-fem Squad room as Science Card 3.
not_performed: No new FEM solves or optimization runs.
No reproduction of the authors' MATLAB optimization.
No verification of motor shape-gradient correctness or speedup.
No claim that the selected motor requires many independent design directions.

prior_art.title: Spline-Based Rotor and Stator Optimization of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
prior_art.findings: Nonlinear 2D model, 22 variables (12 parameters plus 10 surface controls), three current levels and ten rotor angles. Uses adjoints together with radial/axial scaling laws. Reports 120 iterations in six hours. This is an implementation anchor, not a new research idea.
prior_art.reproduction: Pin the published initial geometry, M27 constitutive data, magnet model, winding phases, boundary conditions, sector normalization and torque convention before porting. Distinguish the published v1 snapshot from later repository updates.

prior_art.title: Combined Parameter and Shape Optimization of Electric Machines with Isogeometric Analysis
prior_art.findings: Uses 17 parameters plus 29 symmetric shape variables. Parameter and combined optimization achieve quarter-machine ripple standard deviations 0.0249 and 0.0013 N m at similar mean torque (0.575 and 0.576 N m). These local optima motivate a design-space test, not a proof of dimensional necessity.
prior_art.comparison_limit: The JMAG evolutionary baseline has different objective/constraint settings and slower hardware. Its timing ratio cannot establish an equal-target gradient advantage. Shape-only and sequential cases also relax the torque constraint.
prior_art.cost_lesson: Reported time split: state assembly/solves 65%, objective/derivative calculation 23%, adjoint solves 3%. Counting only linear solves would miss much of the cost.

prior_art.readme: Requires MATLAB plus Optimization, Curve Fitting and Global Optimization toolboxes. Includes GeoPDEs/NURBS dependencies, initial/optimized geometry, material models and saved torque data. GPL-3.0-or-later code; no code copied into GEODE in this screen.
prior_art.local_runtime: Neither matlab nor octave was found on PATH during the audit; gmsh is present. Availability outside PATH was not checked.

available.capability: 2D P1/P2 scalar magnetostatic assembly with prescribed element reluctivity and PM source
Arkkio and Maxwell-stress torque from P1 cell fields
Slotless linear PM motor with analytic torque oracle
Existing oracle and mesh-convergence tests (not rerun in this screen)
3D inductance reluctivity adjoint, useful as a pattern but not a motor shape gradient

not_found_in_audited_source: Nonlinear magnetic B-H residual, consistent Newton tangent and material-data validation.
Slotted iron motor geometry with physical rotor rotation and sliding/mortar coupling.
2D motor torque/ripple discrete shape adjoint including geometry, PM and current-load dependence.
additional_checks: Existing P2 cell-average B recovery cannot simply be fed to a quadratic torque functional and assumed P2-accurate; integrate the field products with appropriate quadrature.
Audit dimensional conventions: existing code includes axial length in torque while some labels say per axial length. Define total N m versus N m/m and sector scaling explicitly for the new benchmark.
A rotating sinusoidal source on a fixed linear operator is not a substitute for moving slotted rotor geometry.

proposed_first_model.geometry: Published ICEM 2D slotted PM motor, initial geometry first; reproduce before changing geometry or bounds.
proposed_first_model.physics: Nonlinear magnetostatics with a differentiable monotone B-H law, permanent magnets and phase windings; synchronous angle snapshots at fixed load angle.
proposed_first_model.operating_points: Use the reference zero/half/full current cases first. Current phase tracks rotor angle. Zero current measures cogging; positive currents measure loaded ripple.
proposed_first_model.objective: F(x) = sum_q w_q mean_k[(T_qk(x)-mean_k T_qk(x))/T_ref]^2, with fixed positive T_ref and predeclared weights. Include zero-current cogging without dividing by its near-zero mean torque.
proposed_first_model.constraints: Per-loaded-condition mean-torque floors, minimum air gap and iron bridge thickness, nonintersecting geometry, bounded magnet area and fixed outer envelope/axial length for the first shape-isolation comparison. Freeze electrical control policy initially.
proposed_first_model.scope: An electromagnetic benchmark. Thermal lifetime, demagnetization, high-speed mechanical qualification and full drive-cycle efficiency are later questions, not implied by these constraints.
design_spaces: A small engineering-parameter subset chosen before optimization; include magnet dimensions and a simple rotor-profile parameter where permitted.
All reference engineering parameters that remain free under fixed-envelope constraints.
The same parameters plus the reference symmetric surface controls.
Only after useful improvement is demonstrated: nested refinements of the same surface basis with a fixed minimum feature size.

execution_gates.deliverable: Initial and published optimized torque waveforms at all reference current levels, pinned geometry/material inputs, independent reference comparison and mesh/angle convergence.
execution_gates.gate: Establish the absolute torque/ripple error floor before setting a target. A stored reference CSV is a cross-check, not a converged ground truth. Reject apparent ripple gains smaller than the numerical uncertainty.

execution_gates.deliverable: Implicit adjoint through the converged nonlinear residual; central-difference step-size sweeps and Taylor tests at initial and perturbed designs, including active loaded conditions and geometry constraints.
execution_gates.gate: Differentiate the same torque functional that is optimized. Use the consistent material tangent, not frozen permeability. Confirm derivative convergence under tighter nonlinear tolerances and spatial/angular refinement. Measure total forward-plus-gradient cost.

execution_gates.deliverable: Matched local optimization in the small and expanded spaces from three fixed feasible starts, initially capped at 20 iterations each and logged as a screening budget, not a converged optimum comparison.
execution_gates.gate: Continue only if added shape freedom produces practically useful, refinement-stable improvements beyond the small basis. If inconclusive at this budget, report inconclusive; do not claim low-dimensional impossibility.
execution_gates.diagnostic: Across perturbed designs, compare the cheap model's predicted changes against FEM changes and examine singular values of the scaled torque-waveform residual Jacobian. A scalar objective's gradient rank is not an effective-dimension test. Charge all calibration calls.

execution_gates.deliverable: Measure same-host elapsed time, CPU-hours and peak memory to a preregistered refined target from matched starts. Compare exact-gradient constrained optimization, calibrated reduced-model search, derivative-free trust-region search, and CMA-ES; add finite differences as a diagnostic rather than the sole baseline.
execution_gates.gate: Report time against the fastest successful credible baseline, with all failures/censoring and target attainment rates. Test 10x as an ambition, not an assumed or required outcome.

fair_accounting: Use the same shape spaces, bounds, targets, material law, physics discretization and starting designs for the optimizer comparison; label the low-dimensional design-space comparison separately.

Count geometry/mesh updates, matrix assembly, nonlinear iterations, factorization, RHS solves, adjoint/derivative assembly, line search, constraint gradients and calibration. Separate shared setup from per-run cost.

Permit warm starts, factor reuse, batched operating points and reduced models for all competitors where valid. Match core limits; report elapsed time and total compute when parallel finite differences or populations are used.

For S operating states, adjoint work is per state and per independent scalar output; it is not one backward solve for the entire motor and every constraint. Aggregate objective and torque constraints transparently.
Validate on denser and shifted angle grids, tighter state tolerances and finer spatial meshes; check intermediate currents withheld from optimization. Fix target/error margins before final timing.
If a method does not reach the target, report its budget and best feasible objective; do not replace that outcome with a fabricated finite speedup.
Existing adjoints already have favorable parameter-count scaling. Automatic differentiation alone does not establish an algorithmic advantage over an established adjoint implementation.
next_concrete_task: Implement and validate nonlinear scalar magnetostatics with a consistent tangent on a small manufactured/material test, then reproduce the published motor's initial torque waveform. The current slotless model cannot answer the optimization question.
stop_conditions: A calibrated simple model reaches the same refined target at comparable or lower total cost.
Useful changes remain confined to a few engineering parameters over the tested design region.
The optimized ripple disappears under denser angle sampling or mesh refinement.
The forward/gradient implementation cost makes this a poor near-term benchmark; retain the negative evidence rather than escalating compute.
